entities.summary:
Ben Stom (1886–1965) was a Dutch footballer of the early professionalising era of association football in the Netherlands. Active when clubs, regional competitions, and a national team culture were crystallising before and after the First World War, he belonged to the first generations who made football a mass spectator sport in Dutch cities.

Early Dutch internationals and club players like Stom helped standardise rules, tactics, and club loyalties that later produced the famous mid-century Total Football lineage. Their significance is foundational rather than stylistic celebrity: building institutions, gates, and popular attachment.

Sports history places him among the pioneers of Dutch football’s organisational takeoff.
